learning_objective: 🎯 Master the super-glue words that connect ideas, sentences, and paragraphs together beautifully!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Conjunctions are the super-glue of English! They stick words, phrases, or full sentences together. Without them, we would sound like robots speaking in short, choppy sentences.
Coordinating conjunctions connect equal ideas. Just remember FANBOYS: For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So. 'I wanted pizza, BUT my mom cooked vegetables.'
Subordinating conjunctions connect a main idea to a dependent idea. Words like 'because', 'although', 'if', and 'when' show a strong relationship. 'We stayed inside BECAUSE it was raining.'
Some conjunctions love to work in pairs! These are called Correlative Conjunctions. Examples include 'either/or' and 'neither/nor'. 'You can have EITHER chocolate OR vanilla.'

fun_activity.title: 🧩 The Super Glue Sentence
fun_activity.instructions: Take two boring sentences: 'I love playing football' and 'I am very tired'. Use the conjunctions 'and', 'but', and 'because' to stick them together in three different ways!

quick_recap: ⭐ Conjunctions join words, phrases, and clauses to make our sentences flow smoothly.
⭐ There are three main types: Coordinating (FANBOYS), Subordinating (like because, when), and Correlative pairs.
